data.narrative:
OpenStar, a Seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Ratu Mataira and Thomas Berry, has raised $35M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), including notable names such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Valuation was derived using stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach. A $10.0B proxy base value anchored to total capital raised was escalated by a 2.5x multiplier, reflecting the typical step-up from Seed to the next financing stage. This produced an implied valuation of $25.0B. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy vertical; while nine same-sector peers exist, fewer than three met narrow stage and tier filters necessary for meaningful cross-sectional analysis.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21.2B (low) to $28.7B (high), with a median of $25.0B. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate stage-to-stage multiplier for this early-stage cohort and the lack of tight peer validation. The single-method dependency and sparse comparable universe at the Seed stage in this sector materially constrain conviction. Additional data on recent Seed-to-Series A outcomes within Climate & Energy would strengthen calibration.
